invariants.description: with clamp_mode = 0 the membrane potential is the integrated one: V = V_ode
every gate and Ca buffer occupancy stays in [0, 1] (to 1e-6, the solver's tolerance on the small SR states); the SR release states R and RI stay >= 0 (R may pass 1: see the next invariant)
the four SR release states R, O, I and RI keep their sum (1.1235 at the CellML's initial values, which do not sum to 1; so R can exceed 1, e.g. 1.0098 at 30 nM ACh)
invariants.expr: np.max(np.abs((R_Ca_SR_release + O + I + RI) - (R_Ca_SR_release + O + I + RI)[0])) <= 1e-6

invariants.description: the cell paces at the run's 10 nM ACh: V crosses -20 mV upward at least 4 times in 2 s, within -75 to +40 mV
at 10 nM ACh the cycle lengths after the first beat are 0.41-0.45 s (from the CellML's initial values, which are for ACh = 0, where the cycle is 0.355 s; Severi et al. 2012 report 352 ms)

bc_sweep.rationale: the one boundary condition, acetylcholine: none (the default, the control model), 1 nM, 10 nM (the run's operating point) and 30 nM, where the cell slows to a cycle of about 0.6-0.7 s. The 115 constants and initial values are the published model's and are not swept: moving each alone by a factor 0.5-2 tests nothing the model was built for.

baseline.reason: candidate: the control action potential features and the ACh rate modulation reported by Severi et al. 2012, digitised; the model is the authors' own CellML, whose control cycle length (0.355 s) the invariants check.

calibrate.note: not_applicable: the published model, used with its own values.
